lines:
ComfyUI workflow tools are native Rust capabilities; the Python MCP bridge, its compilation, its managed server entry and its registration step are deleted.

Functional completion (this turn)
- Registry admission: a workflow tool's descriptor is generated from Settings (comfyui_tool_descriptor) and used for authority-binding identity only; pipeline.rs and continuation.rs add it to the per-Run dynamic descriptors, and FileToolHostPortV1::dispatch_comfyui re-derives and re-checks version/hash against the manifest before executing in process, with a watcher that aborts the queue wait on Run cancellation. No Settings-derived descriptor enters the frozen capability-host registry.
- Fixed the frozen argument shape check: an optional workflow parameter may now be omitted instead of being required by the catch-all arm.
- Native authoring helpers comfyui.list_node_types and comfyui.get_workflow: compile-time schemas, built-in Plugin descriptors, approval-free, frozen endpoint (plus the workflow table for the reader) resolved from Settings; the reader and catalog page are bounded.
- Agent-node offer: toolRegistry lists ComfyUI entries (helpers plus each enabled workflow tool) once a workflow tool exists, and workflowExecution accepts comfyui.<id> tool bindings.
- Deleted: desktop/tool-plugins/comfyui-bridge (tracked package), comfyui/bridge.rs, ComfyUiConfigurationV2.bridgeServerId, settings_v2_comfyui_register plus its Tauri command and the register/activation UI, ComfyUiRegisterResultV2, the bundled-bridge reference-plugin test, and the hand-installed copy under %APPDATA%/com.aworkit.desktop/runtime/tool-plugins/comfyui-bridge. Docs that named the deleted reference plugin now name the FFmpeg bridge.
- Design model: the component is renamed "ComfyUI Workflow Tools and Settings" with a native-tool description, the ComfyUI markdown document is rewritten for the native design, stale bridge bindings are replaced with the new files, and the tool-plugin document no longer claims a ComfyUI reference plugin.

Verification
- cargo check --lib: clean (only the two pre-existing graph_pass warnings).
- cargo test --lib: 557 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. (When USERPROFILE is unset in the agent shell, 102 home-directory-dependent tests fail with "user home directory is unavailable"; that is the shell environment, not the change.)
- New tests: runtime/tool_loop/comfyui_tests.rs runs a stub ComfyUI server end to end - a Settings-derived workflow tool is frozen, admitted through its generated descriptor, dispatched in process, and its produced PNG is stored as image evidence, and an undeclared argument is refused before the server is contacted; plus bounded catalog-page and workflow-reader tests.
- Frontend: tsc --noEmit clean; vitest workbench suites for toolRegistry, mcpSelection, NodeConfigurationForm, SettingsScreen, configuration, settingsV2Port and workflowExecution green; full vitest 618 passed / 3 failed, and the three are pre-existing environment failures (host shell dialect reports powershell on Windows; a locale thousands separator renders 64.192 instead of 64,192).

Make ComfyUI workflow tools native Rust tools, replacing the Python MCP bridge.

WHY
The bridge duplicated logic that already existed in Rust: crates/aworkit-capability-host/src/comfyui.rs ComfyUiClient::{queue_prompt, wait_for_history, view} were unreferenced by the desktop app while comfy_client.py reimplemented them. It also required a host Python interpreter, needed a plugin folder installed at <data_root>/tool-plugins/comfyui-bridge, and surfaced the tools only as one server-level MCP checkbox in the Agent node instead of named tools.

STATE: IN PROGRESS. The tree compiles and the native execution path is complete and tested. Registry admission, authoring helpers and deletion of the Python path remain.

DONE

1. Native tool definitions from Settings — desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/comfyui/tools.rs (new), exported from comfyui/mod.rs
   - capability ids comfyui.<tool id>; comfyui_tool_id / is_comfyui_capability reject foreign ids (bare prefix, mcp://, tool.*)
   - comfyui_native_tools(configuration): one tool per ENABLED workflow tool, in Settings order; a disabled tool does not resolve
   - comfyui_input_schema(tool): model-facing JSON schema generated from the typed parameter list (type, description, default, enum from observed choices, required, additionalProperties:false)
   - comfyui_frozen_configuration(tool, endpoint): endpoint, workflow path and every (node id, input name) binding, frozen per Chat

2. Freeze — desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/service/workflow_tools.rs freeze_graph_bindings
   - a comfyui.<id> branch beside the MCP branch: resolves from settings.comfyui, warns and skips when absent or disabled, pushes FrozenToolBindingV1 with definition: Some(ModelToolDefinitionV1) so the tool reaches the model BY NAME with a per-tool schema

3. Runtime — desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/tool_loop.rs
   - new StoredFileToolLimitV1::ComfyUi { endpoint, workflow_path, parameters }
   - freeze_comfyui_binding: validates the frozen configuration shape and requires the generated definition
   - arms added at the freeze site, the expected-argument-keys site, the typed validation site and the dispatch site
   - tool_approval_copy arm: "Allow ComfyUI workflow run?" with the arguments shown (side effect NonIdempotent)
   - validate_comfyui_arguments: refuses undeclared keys, missing required values, nulls, wrong JSON types and values outside the reported choice set
   - desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/tool_loop/comfyui_tool.rs (new): run_comfyui_tool reads the workflow JSON under a 2 MiB bound, writes only the arguments the model supplied into the frozen (node id, input name) pairs, then ComfyUiClient queue_prompt -> wait_for_history -> view, storing the image through runtime.images.import_bytes as immutable evidence. COMFYUI_WAIT bounds one poll, not a Run.
   - tool_loop/image_tools.rs result_images now recovers images from ComfyUI results, so the produced image reaches the model as vision input

VERIFIED
- cargo check --lib: clean (only the two pre-existing graph_pass.rs warnings)
- cargo test --lib comfyui: 34 tests; one failure was a real bug in first_output_image (serde_json maps iterate in BTreeMap order, so node "12" sorted before "9" and a temp preview beat the saved output). Fixed by preferring type=="output" over "temp"; module re-run: 2 passed, 0 failed.

REMAINING

1. Registry admission (last functional piece). One capability descriptor per frozen ComfyUI tool so the broker admits the call. mcp_tool_descriptor (tool_loop.rs ~1031) is the shape, but MCP bypasses the frozen registry because its dispatch goes through the session manager, whereas ComfyUI dispatches in-process through FileToolDispatcherV1 and must be registered like a built-in (file_tool_descriptors). Needs: locate where a frozen binding resolves its descriptor per Run, then register accordingly.

2. Native authoring helpers: comfyui.list_node_types and comfyui.get_workflow (read-only, CapabilityKind::Plugin), replacing the bridge's comfyui_list_node_types / comfyui_get_workflow.

3. Delete the Python path: desktop/tool-plugins/comfyui-bridge/, comfyui/bridge.rs (materialize_bridge, bridge_server_entry), ComfyUiConfigurationV2.bridge_server_id, the register/probe step in runtime/service/comfyui.rs, the python_program use for the bridge, the register/connect UI in settings-v2/ComfyUiSection.tsx and SettingsScreen.tsx, and the manually installed copy at %APPDATA%/com.aworkit.desktop/runtime/tool-plugins/comfyui-bridge.

4. Tests: a stub ComfyUI server covering freeze -> validation -> execution; retire the bridge tests (bridge.rs and the comfyui-bridge reference-plugin test).

ACCEPTANCE (unchanged): an enabled workflow tool appears by name in the Agent node, executes without Python, its image is recorded as evidence, and deleting the bridge package breaks nothing.

data.title: Make ComfyUI workflow tools native Rust tools (remove the Python bridge)
